title: The Expert System’s Champion
author: Tchaikovsky, Adrian
review: The story went in a direction I wasn't expecting and didn't build off my favorite parts of the first book. Still good writing but didn't quite land completely for me. Reading it back to back it seemed like it didn't quite have continuity with the first one especially in terms of the themes. Almost felt like a different story

highlights.text: The hill, the shielding boulder they’d built against, it was moving. Weed and mud at its base bulged and split as it levered itself up. He saw the vast limbs there, like the hand of a half-formed god.

The thing that killed us was not even the world-stuff itself, but the way our bodies could not abide it. Our blood, our flesh, fought so fiercely against the touch of every part of this world that we consumed ourselves, a man who burns his house down to drive out the vermin that had crept into it.

I lifted my voice, using all the tricks I remembered from Sharskin before me, the ways of speaking that put fire and certainty in people’s hearts. It’s a terrible thing when used for ill, that certainty.
Bain was calling a meeting. Compared to that, the thought of having his brain peaceably devoured by a snail seemed almost merciful,
First lesson of leadership school: always be seen to be doing something. Even when there is nothing to be done.
Sometimes strength is a strange thing, owned by none and yet everyone borrows it from their neighbour.
I am the snail who dreams it is a philosopher, and thinks itself a philosopher dreaming of the snail.”

We all have a council of voices in our minds to prod us forwards or pull us back, but with Leviathan those voices had once been men and women, ancestors who had been devoured, or else entered into a compact with her to save themselves from the killing land.
